description: Rewrite a nested-quantifier email regex vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking so a pathological input can no longer cause exponential blowup
prompts: validator.py's EMAIL_RE pattern `^([a-zA-Z0-9]+)+@[a-zA-Z0-9.]+$` has a nested quantifier - `([a-zA-Z0-9]+)+` - which is classically vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking: a long run of matching characters with no `@` forces the regex engine into exponential-time backtracking before it can fail. Rewrite the pattern to accept exactly the same valid emails and reject the same invalid ones, WITHOUT nested quantifiers that can blow up - a string of 30 'a' characters with no '@' must fail to match near-instantly, not hang.

setup_files.validator.py:
import re

EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r'^([a-zA-Z0-9]+)+@[a-zA-Z0-9.]+$')


def is_valid_email(s):
    return EMAIL_RE.match(s) is not None

reference_solution.validator.py:
import re

EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9.]+@[a-zA-Z0-9.]+$')


def is_valid_email(s):
    return EMAIL_RE.match(s) is not None
